generations.description: First-generation Plymouth Barracuda on the A-body platform. Often referred to as the 'fish-bowl' fastback. Slant-six and 273 V8 power.
Second-generation Barracuda on the redesigned A-body. Notchback, fastback, and convertible body styles. 273/340/383 V8 options including the Formula S package.
Third-generation Barracuda on the E-body platform shared with Dodge Challenger. Big-block era including 340, 383, 440, and 426 Hemi 'Cuda variants. Iconic American muscle car. Final MY 1974.
Plymouth Belvedere mid-size sedan/coupe/wagon on the B-body platform. Donor for the original GTX performance variant. Final MY 1970 before consolidation under Satellite/Road Runner naming.
Plymouth GTX performance variant of the Belvedere/Satellite. 440 Super Commando and 426 Hemi V8 options. 'Gentleman's muscle car' positioning. Final MY 1971.

Plymouth Road Runner muscle coupe on the B-body platform. Cartoon-themed budget muscle car with 383 / 440 / 426 Hemi options. Iconic in muscle car era. Continued on later platforms until final MY 1980.
Plymouth Duster compact coupe on the A-body platform. Slant-six standard, 340/360 V8 in 340/Twister/Feather Duster variants. Final MY 1976 before nameplate retirement.
Plymouth Laser - badge-engineered Mitsubishi Eclipse / Eagle Talon DSM coupe (1G). 4G63T turbo all-wheel-drive variants are popular in the DSM tuning community. Final MY 1994.
